subject: Gift cards are only for gifts
preheader: The gift card scam, passwords that are easy to remember, and AI that compares things.
intro: Today: one rule that protects you from a whole family of scams.

sections.label: Scam of the week
sections.title: Anyone who asks you to pay with gift cards
paragraphs: Banks, government agencies, tech support, and "your grandson" don't take payment in gift cards. Only scammers do.
bullets: If anyone asks you to buy gift cards and read out the numbers, it's a scam. Every time.
Stop and hang up, even if they say it's urgent or a secret.
If you've already paid, call the gift card company straight away using the number on the card. They can sometimes stop the money if you act fast, and tell your bank too.

sections.label: Tip of the week
sections.title: Use three random words as a password
paragraphs: Long beats clever. Three or four unrelated words are easier to remember and much harder to guess than something like "P@ssw0rd1."
bullets: Pick words that don't belong together, like "teapot canyon sneaker."
Use a different one for your email, because email can reset every other account.
Never reuse your email password anywhere else.

sections.label: AI trick of the week
sections.title: Compare two things without the sales pitch
paragraphs: Choosing between two products? Ask AI for the plain pros and cons.
sections.prompt: I'm choosing between a robot vacuum and a regular upright vacuum for a small apartment with one cat. Give me pros and cons of each in plain language.
sections.note: AI can be wrong about prices and specs, so check those on the store's own page.
